newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Prime sees revenue rising in 1997.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Prime sees revenue rising in 1997.

text.p: Prime Television Ltd said on Thursday it was optimistic that it could increase revenue in the 1997 year and that 1997 had started well.
"I'm cautiously optimistic that we will be able to grow revenue in 1997," Prime chief executive George Brown told a briefing for analysts and journalists.
Earlier Prime announced a 21.7 percent rise in its net profit for the six months to December 31 to A$7.98 million and set an unchanged dividend of four cents per share.
Sales rose 20.4 percent to A$60.7 million, but included about six weeks of revenues from the recently acquired Golden West Network.
Prime said its core business revenue, excluding Golden West, rose 13 percent for the period with national sales growing at a faster rate than local sales.
Earnings per share for the period increased to 9.0 cents from 7.7 cents.
"The newly acquired GWN (Golden West) has performed well since acquisition, with revenues and profit running ahead of budget," Prime said.

"At the time of acquisition, directors indicated their belief that Prime Television could increase GWN's EBIT result to A$10.0 million after restructuring, and strategies are being implemented to achieve that objective," it said.
Given the strength of its underlying cash flow, Prime said it believed existing debt levels were comfortable.
Prime's borrowings rose to A$140 million by December 31 from A$75 million at June 30, 1996 to finance the Golden West purchase.
Net interest expense fell to A$3.4 million from A$4.5 million as the debt was incurred late in the period.

"Management continues to search for suitable acquisition opportunities, both in Australia and offshore, so as to position the company to continue to deliver above average growth to shareholders," Prime added.
